title: Judicial Legislation
lead: ==‘When the State fails to perform its constitutional duties, the judiciary must intervene to ensure that the rule of law prevails’ — Justice P.N. Bhagwati.== Judicial legislation stands at the ==razor's edge between justice and jurisdiction==.

head: Case
Year
Judicial creation / principle
rows: Propounded the ==Basic Structure Doctrine== — a new constitutional principle limiting Parliament's power.
==Vishaka Guidelines== on workplace sexual harassment — filled the vacuum until the ==2013 POSH Act==.
Directed ==State Police Commissions and fixed tenures== — a model police reform law.
Mandated ==disclosure of criminal and financial background== of candidates — basis for electoral reform.
Binding directions on ==CBI autonomy== and vigilance structure — led to the ==CVC Act (2003)==.
Created committees against misuse of ==s.498A IPC== — later modified by the SC itself.

head: Aspect
Advantages / justifications
Criticisms / concerns
rows: Fills legal and administrative gaps — ==Vishaka Guidelines protected women before any statute existed==
Judicially crafted rules ==lack democratic legitimacy==, bypassing debate and scrutiny
Holds executive and legislature accountable (Vineet Narain)
Frequent intervention weakens executive responsibility — ==‘government by judiciary’==
Expands Art 21 — right to food, privacy, shelter
Courts overstep into ==policy domains needing legislative expertise==
A ==constitutional safety valve== when Parliament delays ([[Shreya Singhal, 2015]])
Repeated use ==erodes separation of powers== and parliamentary sovereignty
Swift response to technology, environment, gender justice
==Overreach and arbitrariness== — subjective value judgments replace democratic process
Judiciary seen as a ==neutral protector of rights==
==Overreliance dilutes public pressure== on legislature and executive
Legislatures delay codifying — ==temporary judicial law becomes de facto permanent==
Quick remedies where legislative processes are gridlocked
Tension between ==constitutional morality and political morality== — counter-majoritarian excess

items: ==Codify guidelines== — joint criteria on when judicial directions may substitute legislation
==Sunset clauses== — judicial guidelines valid only until a law is enacted
==Legislative responsiveness== — parliamentary committees acting promptly on judicial observations
==Judicial restraint== — the principle of ==constitutional necessity, not convenience==
==Public consultation== — amicus curiae and expert panels before framing policy-like directions

blocks.text: When the legislature sleeps, the judiciary must awaken — but not dream in its place.
